transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
Hello, Dr. Smith. My sleep has been all over the place for weeks, and I can’t seem to get back to anything like a normal schedule.
Besides your sleep issues, have you noticed periods where you feel unusually energetic or talkative, or conversely, times where you feel deeply sad or lose interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yes, I've been swinging back and forth. Some days I feel this heavy, empty sadness where I lose all interest in my jewelry work, but then I'll have these high phases where I'm incredibly energetic and talkative, taking on way too many projects at once because I feel like I can do anything.
During those high phases where you feel incredibly energetic and take on many projects, how many days in a row do those periods typically last?

I'm not entirely sure of the exact number of days they last, as I haven't kept a precise track of the count. They seem to go on for several days or a good stretch of time before I swing back, but when I'm in that zone, time just kind of blurs together.

During those high phases, do you find that your energy level is so intense that it interferes significantly with your ability to work or socialize, or have you ever required hospitalization because of your behavior?

Yes, it absolutely interferes—I start a million things at the shop but get so distracted and restless that nothing gets finished, which led to missed deadlines and a canceled commission. I've also been avoiding church and my bluegrass jams because I'm just too keyed up to sit still. I've never been hospitalized, but my pastor and a close hiking buddy urged me to seek help before things got worse.
During these high phases, have you ever experienced any unusual beliefs that weren't grounded in reality, or heard or seen things that others could not?

No, I've never seen or heard things that aren't there, and I don't think my beliefs are detached from reality. My mind just gets incredibly racing and I get way too confident about what I can pull off with my jewelry work during those times.
When you are in these high-energy phases, do they last for at least one full week, or do they typically resolve in a shorter period of time?

Yes, those high-energy phases definitely last for at least a week, and sometimes they can go on for a couple of weeks at a time. It’s been a big part of these wild swings I’ve been dealing with over the last two months.

latest_inference.note: The patient confirms that the high-energy phases last at least a week and result in significant functional impairment (missed deadlines, social withdrawal). This meets the criteria for a manic episode, shifting the focus from hypomania (F31.0) toward mania. F31.1 remains as the primary candidate, while F31.2 is included to account for potential severity, though the patient denies psychotic symptoms. F31.9 is removed as the clinical picture now aligns with specific manic criteria.
